match-value-invalid.zone: Enter a zone such as ru or corp.internal — letters, digits and hyphens, parts separated by dots.
match-value-invalid.domain: Enter a domain name (example.com) or a subdomain wildcard (*.example.com).
match-value-invalid.domain-glob-position: Wildcard `*` is allowed only as a leading prefix (`*.example.com`).
match-value-invalid.exact-ip: Enter a valid IPv4 or IPv6 address (e.g. 203.0.113.7 or 2001:db8::7).
match-value-invalid.exact-ip-octet-out-of-range: Octet {octet} (position {position}) is out of range. Each octet must be 0–255.
match-value-invalid.exact-ip-this-host: 0.0.0.0/8 and :: mean “this host”, not a destination — a rule cannot name them.
match-value-invalid.exact-ip-broadcast: 255.255.255.255 is the local broadcast used by DHCP and device discovery, not a destination — a rule cannot name it.
match-value-invalid.application: Enter a program name, a name pattern or a full path (e.g. browser.exe, *vpn*.exe, script.ps1).
match-value-invalid.path-star: In a path, * may stand only as the whole last part, \* or /*: the folder with its subfolders. To match programs by name, write a name pattern without a path.
match-value-invalid.path-not-absolute: Write the full path, starting from a drive (C:\), a network share (\\server\share) or /.
match-value-invalid.path-invalid: This path names no program: it contains “..” or a stray “:”, or it is too deep.
match-value-invalid.path-in-other-users-profile: This folder is in another user's profile. A rule decides only for your own programs. To cover each user's own folder, start the path from %LOCALAPPDATA%, %APPDATA% or %USERPROFILE% on Windows, or from ~ on Linux and macOS.
match-value-invalid.path-unknown-variable: A path may start only from your own profile folders: %LOCALAPPDATA%, %APPDATA% or %USERPROFILE% on Windows, ~ on Linux and macOS. Write any other folder in full.
match-value-invalid.subnet: Enter a network such as 10.0.0.0/8 or 2001:db8::/32.
match-value-invalid.ip-range: Enter a range such as 10.0.0.5-10.0.0.40 (both ends of the same family, first ≤ last).
match-value-invalid.is-exact-ip: This is a single address — choose the type “Exact IP”.
match-value-invalid.is-subnet: This is a subnet — choose the type “Subnet (CIDR)”.
match-value-invalid.is-ip-range: This is an IP range — choose the type “IP range”.
match-value-invalid.is-zone: This is a zone — choose the type “Zone”.
match-value-invalid.is-domain: This is a domain name — choose the type “Domain”.
match-value-invalid.is-application: This is a program — choose the type “Application”.
match-value-invalid.network-too-wide: A network wider than /{prefix} cannot be a rule.
match-value-invalid.network-reserved: This network covers loopback, multicast or “this host” addresses, which a rule cannot route.
match-value-invalid.retired-block-flag: “+block” after the value is no longer read. A deny is now written with ! right before the value: {value}
match-value-invalid.deny-mark: The deny mark ! goes once, right before the value, with no space and never together with ?: !example.com.
match-value-invalid.protected-critical-process: A program the system needs for the network, sign-in or the clock: it cannot be denied or sent over the additional route.
match-value-invalid.protected-own-program: A program of this app or the folder it is installed in: it cannot be denied or sent over the additional route.
match-value-invalid.protected-disk-root: The root of a disk holds every program on it: it cannot be denied or sent over the additional route.
match-value-invalid.protected-system-folder: A system folder: its programs cannot be denied or sent over the additional route as a whole. A single program in it can.
match-value-invalid.protected-shared-folder: A folder many programs share: it cannot be denied or sent over the additional route as a whole. Choose the folder of one program inside it.
match-value-invalid.protected-search-path-folder: A folder of the system search path, where unrelated programs sit side by side: it cannot be denied or sent over the additional route as a whole. Choose single programs in it.
match-value-invalid.protected-not-a-plain-path: Not a full path: write it from the drive letter or from /, without “..”.
match-value-invalid.protected-app-path-unsupported: Rules by program path are not applied yet on this system. The rule is kept and will apply once they are; until then, name the program by its file name.

match-value-warning.exact-ip-loopback: Loopback addresses (127.0.0.0/8) are unusual routing targets.
match-value-warning.exact-ip-multicast: Multicast addresses (224.0.0.0/4) are unusual routing targets.
match-value-warning.exact-ip-link-local: Link-local addresses (169.254.0.0/16, fe80::/10) never leave the local network and are unusual routing targets.
match-value-warning.network-wide: Routed, but not blocked when the additional connection drops: leak protection holds networks up to /{prefix}.
match-value-warning.network-wide-public: Routed, but not blocked when the additional connection drops: leak protection holds networks up to /{prefix}. This is a large public network — make sure you meant it.
match-value-warning.single-address: One address: saved as the IP rule {address}.
match-value-warning.protected-file-in-system-folder: A program from a system folder: other parts of the system may rely on it reaching the network.
match-value-warning.override-requested: Not applied: the protection of system programs holds this rule until you confirm it (+override).
match-value-warning.children-not-in-effect: The +children flag is kept but not in effect yet: the rule covers only this program, not the ones it starts

suggestions.body: Without these addresses the sites you routed may not work fully. Checked ones will be added to your rules.

inbox.action-forget-all-tooltip: Removes every suggestion together with your answers, so these addresses can be offered again later.

inbox.title: Addresses your sites need
inbox.intro: These addresses were pulled in by sites you route. Adding one sends it through the additional route together with the site that needs it. Anything you leave alone keeps going through the main route.
inbox.empty-all-inert: The service saw {count} addresses beside your sites, but each already travels the route it would be sent to — a rule would change nothing. For example: {sample}.
inbox.empty: Nothing is waiting for an answer right now.
inbox.load-failed: Could not read the suggestions from the service. Try again in a moment.
inbox.reach: The rule covers every name under {domain}.
inbox.reach-app: The rule sends every connection of {app} through the additional route.
inbox.consumer-on-primary-hint: This site goes through the main route. If you move the address into the tunnel, this site's traffic to it goes there too.
inbox.consumer-copy-hint: Right-click to copy this name to the clipboard.
inbox.behavior-stalls: connections to it stall on the main route
inbox.search-placeholder: Search by domain, host, or site
inbox.select-all-tooltip: Select or clear every address currently shown.
inbox.action-forget-tooltip: Removes the record entirely, answer and all, so the address is offered again if it turns up next to your sites.
inbox.behavior-unknown: not checked on the main route
inbox.sort-main-route: What the main route can't reach first
inbox.action-check-main-route-tooltip: Tries to reach these addresses over the main connection and marks what it finds. Answering there does not mean the site works there — it only means the address is reachable.
inbox.behavior-responds-refusing: the main route reaches it, but the site refuses addresses there
inbox.mark-refusing: This site refuses addresses on the main connection
inbox.mark-refusing-tooltip: Use this when the site opens over the main connection but answers that your address is not served. Its addresses then keep being offered even though they are reachable.
inbox.show-dismissed-tooltip: Also list the addresses you told the app not to suggest again, so you can change your mind about one.
inbox.empty-but-answered: Nothing is waiting for an answer. {n} address(es) you answered earlier are hidden — turn on "Show answered" to revisit one.
inbox.show-served-by-main-link: Show ones the main connection already handles ({n})
inbox.show-served-by-main-link-tooltip: These addresses answer over your main connection, so sending them through the additional one changes nothing. They are listed for completeness, not as work.

inbox.ownership-own-name: one of the site's own names

table.intro: Every address below was pulled in by a site you route. Adding one sends it through the additional route together with the site that needs it — anything you leave alone keeps going through the main route. A dismissed address only stops being offered; "Allow again" lifts that suppression and nothing else.

accept.reload-page: The rule is applied. Reload the page you were on (F5) so it picks up the new route.

main-route.answered-tooltip: Something answered at this address over the main connection. That does not mean the site works there — it may still refuse to serve you. Checked within the last half hour.
main-route.silent-tooltip: Nothing answered at this address over the main connection, so this rule is doing real work. Checked within the last half hour.
main-route.no-address-tooltip: Nothing has visited this address on this computer since the service started, so there is nothing to try. Open the site once and check again.
main-route.unclear-tooltip: The check could not be made: the main connection has no address right now, or the attempt failed to start. Try again later.
main-route.zone-tooltip: A zone covers every site under it, so there is no single address to try.
main-route.action-check-tooltip: Tries to reach the addresses of your additional-route rules over the main connection, and shows the result in the Main route column. Answering there does not mean the site works there — a rule may still be earning its place.
main-route.check-started: Checking {count} addresses over the main connection...
main-route.check-progress: Checking addresses over the main connection: {done} of {total}...
main-route.check-done: Main route check finished: reaches {answered}, does not reach {silent}, not checked {other}.
main-route.check-nothing: Nothing to check: these addresses were checked recently, or none of them has been resolved yet.
main-route.nothing-to-check: There are no additional-route address rules to check.

rules.invalid-count: {n} rule(s) will not be applied: the value is not valid.

vm.intro: A virtual machine's traffic leaves your computer as the traffic of its hypervisor, so the route is chosen for the hypervisor and applies to all of its machines. Changes go to your rules list, where you review and apply them.
vm.scan-failed: Could not read the virtual machines. Try Refresh.
vm.added-note: The rules are in your rules list. Review and apply them there.
vm.route-none: {hypervisor} carries its machines' traffic in a system service, so no program rule can route it.

pin.rules: This machine follows your rules: sites from the rules take their route, everything else goes over {route}.
pin.additional: All of this machine's traffic goes over {route}.
pin.missing: This machine is tied to {address}, which your computer no longer has, so it has no network. Power it off and tie it again.
pin.note: The change is made in VirtualBox and works only while the machine is powered off. If {route} reconnects with a new address, tie the machine again.

error.not-mutable: The machine is running or suspended. Shut it down completely and try again.
error.tool-missing: VBoxManage was not found. Reinstall VirtualBox or change the machine in VirtualBox itself.
error.no-address: {route} has no IPv4 address right now. Connect it and try again.
error.failed: The machine could not be changed.

vm.route-scope: {hypervisor} runs every machine as one program ({processes}), so a route applies to all of its machines.
vm.route-now-mixed: The rules send {hypervisor}'s programs over different routes.
vm.route-now-block: The rules deny the traffic of every {hypervisor} machine.
vm.no-adapters: This machine has no network adapters.
vm.nat-dns: For your site rules to work inside this machine, set its DNS server to {address}.
vm.nat-enable-first: For your site rules to work inside this machine, first let this adapter reach your computer: power the machine off and run the command below. Then set the machine's DNS server to {address}.

overlaps.intro: When rules of the two routes cover the same sites or addresses, the narrower rule wins: an exact name beats a wildcard, a wildcard beats a zone, a longer name beats a shorter one; an exact address beats a subnet or range, a smaller network beats a larger one. Check that each item below goes where you want it to: confirm it, or send it over the other route. Changes go to your rules list, where you review and apply them.
overlaps.nested: {winner} goes over {winner-route}: it is narrower than {loser} on {loser-route}.
overlaps.duplicate: {winner} is set on both routes. It goes over {winner-route}: on a tie the main route wins.
overlaps.block-tie: {winner} names the same sites as {loser} on {loser-route}. They are denied: on a tie a deny wins over a route.
overlaps.block-tie-warning: The other rule names the same sites and never applies.
overlaps.main-stays: Addresses of the main link inside this network stay on the main link even when the additional link is down. Leak protection does not block them.
overlaps.block-note: A deny rule is part of this pair; change it in the rules list.
overlaps.empty: No rules of the two routes cover the same sites or addresses.

conflicts.title: Conflicts in the applied rules
conflicts.hint: Rules the service enforces differently from how they read, as it enforces them now. They update after you apply changes.
conflicts.literal-block: {rule}: {host} resolves to {ip}, and a deny of that address wins over any name rule, so the address is denied.
conflicts.leak: {rule} does not deny {host}: it shares {ip} with {via}, which a narrower rule routes, so the address stays open.
conflicts.unsupported-shape: {rule} for {app} is not enforced: a rule that limits an address to one application cannot be carried out yet, so it is skipped rather than applied to every application.
conflicts.carving-over-cap: {rule} holds more narrower rules than can be carved out of it, so it is not fully enforced, and the narrower rules inside it keep working. Split it into smaller networks.
conflicts.override-pending: The rule {rule} asks to apply despite the protection and is not applied until you confirm it in the rules list. {reason}
conflicts.folder-over-cap: {rule} covers the first {count} programs of its folder. The folder holds more, and those are not covered: name the folder of the program you mean instead.
conflicts.other-users-folder: The rule {rule} is not applied: its folder is in another user's profile, and a rule decides only for its owner's programs. To cover each user's own folder, start the path from %LOCALAPPDATA%, %APPDATA% or %USERPROFILE% on Windows, or from ~ on Linux and macOS.

overlaps.intersecting: {winner} and {loser} on {loser-route} share some addresses. Each shared address takes the narrower rule; most of them go over {winner-route}.
overlaps.send-over-whole: This moves the whole rule, including addresses the other rule does not cover.

conn-trace.title: Connection trace

The list refreshes on its own while it is open and is kept in memory only. (Writing connections to the on-disk log stays an opt-in in Settings.) Shows TCP/UDP connections — a ping (ICMP) leaves no connection to observe, so a pinged address will not appear here.

conn-trace.entries-no-match: No connections match the current filters
conn-trace.learned-route: First connection held at %1 while the address was being learned, then sent over the additional route
conn-trace.remote-hosts-tip: Names this address was answered for (%1):
conn-trace.via-fake-ip: Via fake-IP: a virtual address the service gave this name.
conn-trace.fake-ip-recycled-tip: A virtual (fake-IP) address. The name it stood for is no longer in the pool.
conn-trace.col-process-tip: The application that opened the connection. Hover a row's process name to see its full path.
conn-trace.col-remote-tip: The destination address and port the connection went to. Below it, the name this address was answered for, when one was seen; "(+N)" means N more names share the address — hover the name for the full list.
conn-trace.col-egress-tip: Which network link the connection actually left through: Primary (your main link), Additional (the additional link, usually a VPN), Loopback (local, never leaves the PC), Other (another adapter), Unknown (couldn't be determined). This is observation only — it never changes routing.
conn-trace.col-verdict-tip: Whether the connection was allowed or dropped. A "Blocked" row may be a drop by the system firewall or an antivirus — not necessarily NetRuleRouter.
conn-trace.show-local-tip: Connections to your own machine or your local network (loopback, link-local, private LAN addresses). They never leave your network, so they say nothing about routing.
conn-trace.group-by-tip: By folder: programs of one folder and of the folders inside it form one group, and the group offers a rule for the whole folder.
conn-trace.leak-mismatch-tip: Mismatch: this address belongs to a rule routed to the additional adapter, but the connection was allowed out over the PRIMARY link — a leak indicator.
conn-trace.verdict-note: "Blocked" means the connection was dropped by a filter in the system — this can be the system firewall or your antivirus, not necessarily NetRuleRouter. NetRuleRouter never blocks traffic on your primary route.
conn-trace.observer-unavailable: The service is not observing connections right now, so this list stays empty. The service log says why.
conn-trace.auto-paused: Paused — scroll to the top or clear the selection to resume
conn-trace.gui-stream-off: Showing the connection trace is switched off in Settings → Diagnostics and logs. Observation itself keeps running.
conn-trace.card-summary: Which interface each outgoing connection actually left through.
conn-trace.only-ipv6-tip: Show only connections made over IPv6. They are observed, but routing rules do not apply to that family yet — so these are the connections currently travelling outside your policy. Link-local IPv6 counts as local, so tick "Show local connections" as well to see it.

Sites can refuse to sign you in through it. Check the HTTPS scanning settings of your antivirus, or open the site over the other route.

route-down.body: The connection the site is routed over is down or not connected, so nothing reaches the site that way. Reconnect it, or check Interfaces and routes.

blocked.body: A deny rule in your rules holds the site, so nothing is sent to it. Change or remove that rule in Rules if the site should open.

cookies.edge: Edge: click the icon left of the address, open "Cookies and site data", and delete the site's cookies.

event.dns-refresh-loopback-pinned: DNS refresh: {hostname} resolved only to a loopback/unspecified address (hosts file?) — not cached, retrying in {retry_in_secs}s
event.dns-refresh-unsupported-platform: DNS refresh: the resolver is not supported on this platform ({reason}) — aborting this refresh tick
event.dns-refresh-upsert-failed: DNS refresh: saving a resolved entry to the cache failed ({error})
event.dns-refresh-record-failure-failed: DNS refresh: recording a failed resolution for {hostname} failed ({error})
event.dns-upstream-rotated: The upstream DNS server stopped answering — switched from {retired} to {active}
event.dns-upstream-reselected: Upstream DNS server re-selected after a network change: {previous} -> {active}
event.dns-upstream-worker-spawn-failed: Could not start the background worker for upstream DNS re-selection ({error})
event.doh-baseline-seeded: Seeded the DoH/DoT resolver baseline with {seeded} entries on first run
event.doh-baseline-seed-failed: Seeding the DoH/DoT resolver baseline failed (non-fatal): {error}
event.doh-baseline-seed-updated: Added {added} new entries to the DoH/DoT resolver baseline from built-in list version {version}
event.doh-baseline-seed-retired: Removed {removed} withdrawn entries from the DoH/DoT resolver baseline per built-in list version {version}
event.persid-plan-app-rules-delivered: Application rules delivered to enforcement: primary {primary_app_rules}, additional {secondary_app_rules}.
event.persid-plan-unresolved-hosts-dns-query: {hosts} rule host(s) have no confirmed address yet; asking DNS to resolve them now instead of waiting ({dropped} additional host(s) skipped this round).
event.persid-plan-app-rules-unresolved: {count} application rule(s) are not enforced: no installed or running program matched ({apps}).
event.persid-plan-vpn-client-awaiting-confirma: {count} program(s) named like a VPN client sit outside the protected program folders ({apps}); they stay under leak protection until confirmed as the link provider.
event.vpn-gateway-awaiting-confirmation: Leak protection stopped what looks like another VPN reaching its server {address}; the user is asked whether to let it through.
event.persid-plan-app-claimed-by-main: {count} application rule address(es) overlap with main-link rules and stay on the main link ({conflicts}); the app keeps the additional link for everything else.
event.persid-plan-app-dest-shared: {count} application rule address(es) are used by other programs too, so they stay off the additional link and the application reaches them over the main link ({conflicts}).
event.persid-plan-app-dest-shared-guarded: {count} application rule address(es) are used by other programs too, so they stay off the additional link; with leak protection on, the application cannot reach them ({conflicts}).
event.persid-plan-app-rules-overcapped: {count} application rule(s) are only partially enforced: more matching programs were found than the per-app limit allows ({apps}).
event.persid-plan-rule-shape-unsupported: {count} rule(s) are not enforced: they limit an address to one application, which cannot be carried out yet, so they were skipped rather than applied to every application ({rules}).
event.persid-plan-suffix-truncated: Rule {rule_id} for suffix {suffix} matched more hosts than the limit of {cap}; only the most recently seen hosts were enforced.
event.persid-plan-pin-set-trimmed: Leak protection address set trimmed: {kept} address(es) kept, {dropped} dropped (already routed elsewhere or covered by {app_covered} app-observed destination(s)).
event.persid-plan-shared-ip-excluded: Leak protection leaves {excluded} address(es) shared with other sites out of blocking; {pinned} address(es) stay held.
event.persid-plan-service-dns-spared: Additional-link rules name {count} DNS server(s) of the main link ({servers}). System services keep reaching them over the main link: cutting them would break name resolution for the whole machine. The local DNS resolver moves name resolution to the service.
event.persid-service-accounts-owner-changed: Users the route table serves changed ({previous} → {owner}): system services now follow their leak protection addresses.
event.persid-plan-network-too-wide: {count} network(s) routed through the additional adapter are wider than /{widest_prefix}, so leak protection does not block them while that adapter is down: their traffic may leave through the main adapter (for example: {sample}).
event.foreign-tunnel-networks-over-cap: {count} network(s) of other VPN tunnels are past the limit of {cap} per tunnel and address family and stay under leak protection while the additional adapter is down.
event.persid-plan-network-over-cap: {count} network(s) routed through the additional adapter are past the leak protection limit and are not blocked while that adapter is down (for example: {sample}).
event.persid-plan-network-spared: Leak protection never blocks {count} network(s) routed through the additional adapter: they cover the local network, a reserved range or the tunnel server, or the main adapter's rules name them too (for example: {sample}).
event.persid-plan-kill-switch-active: Leak protection active: {kill_switch_filters} filter(s) pinning {pinned_addresses} address(es).
event.persid-plan-secondary-unresolved-fail-cl: The additional connection could not be found; leak protection holds traffic until it returns ({fail_closed_filters} filter(s)).
event.persid-plan-secondary-unresolved-heartbe: The additional connection is still not found after {elapsed_minutes} minute(s); leak protection keeps holding traffic ({fail_closed_filters} filter(s)).
event.persid-plan-standing-filter-alarm: Standing filter count reached {filters}, above the alarm level (previous peak {previous_peak}): {by_band}.
event.persid-plan-standing-filter-recovered: Standing filter count dropped back to {filters}, below the alarm threshold.
event.persid-plan-machine-filter-alarm: Standing filters on the computer, all users together, reached {filters} (previous peak {previous_peak}), above the alarm threshold.
event.persid-plan-machine-filter-recovered: Standing filters on the computer dropped back to {filters}, below the alarm threshold.
event.persid-apply-phantom-filters: After applying, {phantom} of {expected} filter(s) recorded as installed are not actually active — real enforcement is weaker than reported.
event.persid-apply-recompile-not-enforced: A recompile was asked for a user who holds no filter set and is not enforced right now ({sid}); nothing was installed.
event.persid-apply-settle-recompile-failed: Recompiling the filter set for {sid} after the enforced-users update failed ({error}).
event.persid-apply-reconcile-sid-failed: The enforced-users update failed for {sid} at {stage} ({error}); the other users were still processed.
event.persid-apply-membership-unknown: Could not decide which users hold a filter set ({error}); every set was left as it is.
event.persid-apply-verify-enumerate-failed: Could not check which filters are actually active after applying ({error}); the verification step was skipped.
event.persid-apply-adds-refused-teardown: Shutting down: new filters were not added at stage "{stage}" because a filter added now would outlive this process.
event.persid-apply-best-effort-skipped: Filters applied on a best-effort basis: {installed} installed, {skipped} rule(s) could not be enforced on this machine.
event.persid-apply-delete-superseded-failed: Could not remove {deferred} superseded filter(s) this cycle ({error}); they remain tracked and removal will retry automatically.
event.persid-apply-delete-deferred: Removal of {deferred} superseded filter(s) was postponed this cycle because a replacement block could not be added yet; retrying next cycle.
event.persid-apply-cleanup-delete-failed: Could not remove all tracked filters during cleanup ({error}); some may remain until the next attempt.
event.persid-apply-cleanup-stripped: All filters removed: {tracked_deleted} tracked filter(s) plus {swept} found by a full sweep.
event.persid-apply-cleanup-orphans-failed: Could not remove leftover filters from a previous run ({error}); they may still be present.
event.persid-apply-cleanup-orphans-cleared: Startup cleanup: cleared {ledger_ids} filter reference(s) left from the previous run.
event.persid-apply-dns-flush-ok: DNS cache cleared after a rule change so affected hosts are looked up again instead of using a stale address.
event.persid-apply-dns-flush-failed: Could not clear the DNS cache after a rule change ({error}); affected hosts may keep using a stale address until it expires.
event.persid-apply-install-removed-superseded: Installation removed {removed} filter(s) superseded by the new set.
event.persid-apply-delete-superseded-install-f: Could not remove {superseded} superseded filter(s) during installation ({error}); they may remain until the next cleanup.
event.persid-apply-flows-torn-down: Reset {torn_down} existing connection(s) to {destinations} destination(s) so they reconnect over the correct route (tunnel just came up: {tunnel_came_up}).
event.persid-registry-reconcile-failed: Could not synchronize enforcement with the active user list ({error}); some changes may not have taken effect.
event.persid-registry-policy-paused-skip: Policy changed for a user whose routing is paused; filters were not reapplied because protection is paused for them.
event.persid-registry-policy-recompiled: Routing policy changed; recompiled the filter set for the active user ({filter_count} filter(s)).
event.persid-registry-recompile-failed: Could not recompile the filter set after a routing policy change ({error}); the previous filters remain in effect.
event.persid-posture-dns-flush-ok: DNS cache cleared after leak protection's block-all posture changed (now armed: {block_all_armed}); previously cached names will be looked up again.
event.persid-posture-dns-flush-failed: Could not clear the DNS cache after leak protection's block-all posture changed (now armed: {block_all_armed}): {error}; already-cached names stay unobserved until they expire.
event.persid-posture-dns-flush-link-edge-faile: Could not clear the DNS cache as the additional route went down or came back: {error}; cached answers outlive the change until they expire.
event.persid-posture-app-rules-learning: New application rule(s) delivered for the first time ({apps}); their destinations are still being learned.
event.persid-posture-cross-set-duplicates: {count} active rule(s) name the same traffic on both routes (example: {sample}).
event.persid-shadow-plan-differs: Internal consistency check found a difference between the experimental and live filter plans ({live} live vs {neutral} experimental); live enforcement is unaffected. Only live: {differs_live}. Only experimental: {differs_neutral}.
event.persid-plan-route-table-unreadable: Could not read the system route table; the full block-all protection cannot be armed this round: {error}.
event.persid-plan-links-unreadable: Could not read the list of network adapters; the full block-all protection cannot be armed this round: {error}.
event.persid-plan-blanket-block-refused: Full block-all was requested, but the tunnel server's address could not be determined; arming it would prevent the tunnel from reconnecting, so it was not enabled.
event.persid-plan-blanket-block-no-main-link: Full block-all was requested, but the main link is not resolved; without its local networks the block would cut the local network, so it was not enabled.
event.persid-plan-state-db-unreadable: The policy database could not be opened ({error}); no policy can be enforced until this is resolved.
event.persid-plan-fqdn-cache-unreadable: The domain-name cache could not be opened ({error}); domain-based rules will not resolve until this is fixed.
event.persid-plan-fqdn-cache-migration-failed: The domain-name cache could not be upgraded ({error}); domain-based rules will not resolve until this is fixed.
event.fakeip-stale-flow-swept: Startup cleanup found {found} leftover fake-IP connection(s) and closed {torn_down} of them.
event.fakeip-start-deferred-zombies: Fake-IP start delayed — waiting for {zombies} previous session(s) to finish shutting down.
event.fakeip-start-no-factory: Fake-IP could not start because it was not configured — the feature stays off.
event.fakeip-start-build-failed: Fake-IP could not start because its network component could not be built — the feature stays off.
event.fakeip-run-loop-exited: Fake-IP stopped unexpectedly due to a device error ({error}) — it will not work until it is restarted.
event.fakeip-stack-started: Fake-IP started — virtual addresses are now active.
event.fakeip-shutdown-signal-failed: Fake-IP's stop signal failed to send ({error}) — it may take longer to stop.
event.fakeip-stack-stopped: Fake-IP stopped — names now resolve to real addresses again.
event.fakeip-stop-grace-exceeded: Fake-IP did not stop within {grace_ms} ms and was detached; it will finish stopping in the background.
event.fakeip-thread-self-exited: Fake-IP had stopped running unexpectedly and was cleaned up.
event.fakeip-zombie-reaped: A previous fake-IP session finished shutting down — it can now be restarted.
event.fakeip-relay-dial-activity: Fake-IP relay activity: TCP {tcp_flows_opened} opened ({tcp_dial_ok} ok, {tcp_dial_refused} refused, {tcp_dial_failed} failed), UDP {udp_flows_opened} opened ({udp_dial_ok} ok, {udp_dial_refused} refused, {udp_dial_failed} failed, {udp_unreachable_sent} unreachable).
event.fakeip-datapath-not-running: Fake-IP is enabled but not currently running (waiting on {zombies} lingering process(es)) — traffic protection is inactive until it restarts.
event.fakeip-wedge-cooldown: Fake-IP still appears stuck, but a rebuild just ran — waiting before trying again.
event.fakeip-datapath-wedged-rebuild: Fake-IP appears stuck ({answers_delta} addresses issued but no traffic received) — rebuilding it now.
event.fakeip-flow-worker-start-failed: Could not start the connection-activity worker ({error}) — some route suggestions may be missed.
event.fakeip-flow-notices-dropped: {dropped} connection-activity notice(s) were dropped because processing fell behind.
event.fakeip-vpn-flow-platform-infra: A VPN client ({image}) reached shared service infrastructure at {hostname} — left it in fake-IP mode.
event.fakeip-vpn-flow-healed: Detected VPN client {image} connecting to its server {hostname} through the relay — excluded that server from address substitution and refreshed DNS so it connects directly.
event.fakeip-workers-lingering: {lingering} fake-IP upstream connection(s) are stuck closing — the remote side may be unresponsive.
event.fakeip-flow-capacity-reached: Fake-IP has reached its connection limit ({active} of {cap}) — new connections are refused until some finish.
event.fakeip-udp-flow-capacity-reached: Fake-IP has reached its UDP flow limit ({active} of {cap}) — new UDP clients are refused until some go idle.
event.fakeip-flows-reset-after-rule-change: Reset {flows} relayed connection(s) whose rule changed — the application reconnects under the new rule.
event.fakeip-dial-pool-refused: Fake-IP cannot start another outgoing connection ({reason}; {refused} refused so far) — the connection is reset.
event.fakeip-poll-step-panicked: An internal error interrupted one fake-IP processing step ({reason}) — it was contained and the relay keeps running.
event.mutation-tokens-capped: Too many unconfirmed rule previews ({held} for one user, {total} in all) — the oldest are dropped; confirming one of those asks for a fresh preview.
event.app-observations-app-cap: Application observation limit reached ({cap} programs) — the program seen least recently is forgotten first.
event.app-observations-foreign-shed: Learnt application destinations inside a network another VPN now carries were dropped ({destinations}).
event.fakeip-dial-connected: Connected to {hostname} at {upstream} via {route} in {elapsed_ms} ms.
event.fakeip-dial-failed: Could not connect to {hostname} at {upstream} via {route} after {elapsed_ms} ms: {error}.
event.fakeip-dial-next-address: {hostname} did not answer at {failed}; connected via {route} at {connected} instead ({tried} addresses tried).
event.fakeip-dial-held-succeeded: Connected to {hostname} via {route} after waiting {elapsed_ms} ms for the route to become available ({attempts} attempt(s)).
event.fakeip-dial-policy-refused: Connection to {hostname} via {route} was refused by routing policy after {elapsed_ms} ms ({attempts} attempt(s)): {error}.
event.fakeip-udp-dial-policy-refused: UDP connection to {hostname} via {route} was refused by routing policy after {elapsed_ms} ms: {error}.
event.route-secondary-luid-zero: The additional route's network interface (index {ifindex}) resolved to an invalid identifier — leak protection stays off.
event.route-secondary-luid-error: Could not resolve the identifier of the additional route's network interface (index {ifindex}): {error} — leak protection stays off.
event.route-no-policy-for-user: No routing configuration found for this user — no additional routes will be applied.
event.route-adapter-enum-failed: Could not list network adapters ({error}) — routing targets cannot be resolved right now.
event.route-no-secondary-bound: No additional-route adapter is assigned — assign both connections in "Interfaces & routes" and apply (elevation required); otherwise nothing is routed over the additional connection.
event.route-local-network-too-wide: {adapter} reports {network} as a connected network — too wide to be a local network; it is not exempted from leak protection.
event.route-primary-derived: No main-route adapter is assigned — it was inferred from the system's default route (interface {ifindex}, gateway {gateway}), so unmatched traffic uses the real connection instead of the additional route.
event.route-primary-no-way-out: The main connection (interface {ifindex}) has no gateway and no route out — traffic the rules do not route follows the system's default route instead.
event.route-no-primary-derivable: No main-route adapter is assigned and none could be inferred from the system's default route (additional-route interface {secondary_ifindex}) — in "direct" mode, unmatched traffic stays on the additional route. Assign a main-route adapter in "Interfaces & routes".
event.route-mac-anchor-remembered: Remembered the hardware address of the {role} adapter "{adapter}" so it is still recognized after it changes identifiers.
event.route-local-networks-unreadable-addition: Could not read the system route table ({error}) — reporting no local networks for the additional route.
event.route-local-networks-unreadable-screen: Could not read the system route table ({error}) — the local networks screen will show nothing.
event.route-binding-healed-by-name: The saved {role} adapter ({stale_id}) was no longer found; automatically matched it to "{healed_adapter}" ({healed_id}) by name and saved the correction.
event.route-binding-down-no-heal: The {role} adapter ({stable_id}) is present but not usable right now (status: {oper_status}, has address: {has_ipv4}) and no matching adapter could be found — routing for it is stopped.
event.route-binding-not-found: The saved {role} adapter "{display_name}" ({bound}) was not found among the current network adapters — routing for it is stopped.
event.route-binding-no-next-hop: The {role} adapter "{effective_adapter}" (interface {ifindex}) is up but has no gateway, and no next hop could be determined — it cannot be used for routing.
event.route-no-active-rules: No active rules for this user — no additional routes will be applied.
event.route-counter-overlay-live: Active override route: {destination} via interface {ifindex}, next hop {next_hop}, metric {metric} (on additional route: {on_secondary}).
event.route-counter-overlay-missing: No override routes are active — traffic that should use the main connection may still be using the additional route.
event.route-orphan-enum-failed: Could not read the system route table while recovering routes from a previous run ({error}).
event.route-orphans-adopted: Recovered {count} route(s) left over from a previous run.
event.route-table-owner-changed: The system's own traffic now follows this user's routes.
event.route-table-owner-none: Nobody is signed in: the system's own traffic follows no user's routes.
event.per-user-routing-unsupported: This kernel cannot route each user separately ({reason}): the system route table carries the routes of one signed-in user for everyone.
event.linux-foreign-rule-moved: A routing rule added after the service's (a VPN connected later) stood in front of them; moved from priority {from} to {to}, where it would have been without the service.
event.linux-foreign-rule-ahead: A routing rule far in front of the service's sends all traffic to another table (priority {priority}, table {table}): it is looked up before any user's own routes.
event.linux-foreign-rule-move-failed: A routing rule in front of the service's could not be moved ({error}): until it is, it takes the traffic before the rules do.
event.own-traffic-mark-failed: The service could not mark its own connections ({error}): system-wide filters may hold its checks and lookups.
event.source-link-pin-failed: The service could not hold an external address check to its adapter ({error}): the answer may describe another connection.
event.route-killswitch-luid-error: Leak protection: could not resolve the additional route's interface identifier (index {ifindex}): {error} — staying off.
event.route-killswitch-table-unreadable: Leak protection: could not read the system route table, so local-network exceptions are unknown ({error}) — staying off.
event.route-failclosed-table-unreadable: Leak protection: could not read the system route table ({error}) — falling back to the last known local networks.
event.route-failclosed-cached-subnets: Leak protection: using the last known {subnet_count} local network(s) so the block keeps the LAN reachable.
event.route-secondary-liveness-dead: The additional route's tunnel (interface {ifindex}, next hop {next_hop}) has been unreachable for {window_secs} second(s) — treating it as down and blocking traffic, even though the adapter still looks up.
event.route-first-contact-install-failed: Could not install the immediate route for a newly seen address ({error}) — it will be added on the next routing update.
event.route-no-routing-user: No user to route for right now ({active_count} active) — removing additional routes.
event.route-users-conflict: Another signed-in user already routes {count} of this user's destinations ({addresses}) through a different link. They keep those routes; with leak protection on, this user's traffic to them is blocked rather than sent the other way.
event.route-users-conflict-cleared: The route conflict with another signed-in user is over — this user's routes are in the table again.
event.route-paused-teardown: Routing is paused for this user (remove-on-pause) — removing additional routes.
event.route-paused-persist: Routing is paused for this user (keep-on-pause) — keeping the rule-specific routes and removing only the routes that steered the rest of the traffic.
event.route-policy-recomputed: Routes recomputed after a policy change: {added} added, {removed} removed.
event.route-policy-recompute-failed: Recomputing routes after a policy change failed ({error}).
event.prod-settings-enforcement-mode-written: DNS enforcement mode set to {written} (previous: {prior}, changed: {changed}, live resolver available: {resolver_live}).
event.prod-settings-verbose-logging-written: Verbose service logging set to {written} (previous: {prior}, changed: {changed}, live reload: {live_reload}).
event.prod-settings-conn-trace-log-written: Connection trace log set to {written} (previous: {prior}, changed: {changed}, forced: {forced}, live reload: {live_reload}).
event.prod-settings-dns-via-secondary-written: “DNS through the tunnel” setting saved as {written} (previous: {prior}, changed: {changed}).
event.prod-settings-fast-dns-answers-written: Fast DNS answers setting saved as {written} (previous: {prior}, changed: {changed}).
event.prod-settings-fake-ip-udp-relay-written: Fake-IP UDP relay setting saved as {written} (previous: {prior}, changed: {changed}).
event.prod-settings-rules-lock-written: Administrative rules lock saved as {written} (previous: {prior}, changed: {changed}, requested: {requested}).
event.prod-settings-fake-ip-instant-rst-writte: Fake-IP instant reset setting saved as {written} (previous: {prior}, changed: {changed}).
event.prod-mutation-execute-started: Mutation execute started (kind: {kind}, correlation: {correlation_id}, payload size: {payload_size} bytes).
event.prod-mutation-locked: Mutation refused: rule changes are locked by the administrator (kind: {kind}).
event.prod-mutation-security-alert-active: Mutation refused: a security alert must be acknowledged first (kind: {kind}).
event.prod-mutation-preset-parsed: Preset bytes parsed on the service (route: {route}, known sections: {known_sections}, known rules: {known_rules}, unknown sections: {unknown_sections}, unknown rules: {unknown_rules}).
event.prod-preset-candidate-submitted: Preset candidate submitted (revision: {revision_id}, content hash: {content_hash}). A deduplicated id equal to an existing or active revision means no new rules were detected.
event.provisioning-applied: Installation files applied to the shared rules and settings (rules: {rules}, settings: {policy}).
event.provisioning-refused: Installation files refused: {part} ({code}): {detail}. The shared rules were left as they were.
event.provisioning-mark-failed: Installation files could not be marked as processed: {error}. The next start reads them again.
event.prod-preset-assembled: Preset assembled into a canonical rule book (size: {rules_json_len} bytes, content hash: {content_hash}). An empty book serializes to about 50 bytes.
event.prod-alert-resign-adopted-tampered: Tamper-alert acknowledgement re-signed revision rows that did not match their stored signature; their current contents are now trusted (alert: {alert_id}, re-signed: {re_signed}, adopted: {adopted}, revisions: {revisions}).
event.prod-alert-resign-ok: Revision rows re-signed after tamper-alert acknowledgement (alert: {alert_id}, re-signed: {re_signed}).
event.prod-alert-resign-failed: Re-signing revisions after tamper-alert acknowledgement failed (alert: {alert_id}, error: {error}).
event.prod-alert-adopt-skipped: The acknowledgement named rows it did not trust: changed since they were shown ({changed}) or not covered by this alert ({ignored}) (alert: {alert_id}).
event.prod-activation-already-active: Submitted content matches the active revision; nothing to activate (revision: {revision_id}).
event.prod-activation-reactivate-historical: Submitted content matched a historical revision; re-activating it (revision: {revision_id}, previous status: {status}).
event.prod-rules-json-parse-failed: Canonical rules-JSON parse failed; treating as no active rules (origin: {origin}, error: {error}).
event.prod-rules-codec-decode-failed: Rules-JSON codec decode failed; treating as no active rules (origin: {origin}, error: {error}).
event.stored-rules-not-applied: {kept} stored rule(s) are kept but not applied: an address that is never a destination (this host or broadcast), or an application name that is too long, contains a control character or matches every process. The rules list shows them as not working; the other rules are in force (origin: {origin}).
event.protected-rules-not-applied: {count} rule(s) not applied: they deny a system program or folder, send one over the additional route, or name a program by a path this system cannot apply yet ({rules}).
event.protection-override-read-failed: Confirmed rules could not be read; none of them applies (error: {error}).
event.protection-override-no-key: {count} confirmed rule(s) are not honoured this start: the signing key is unavailable, so the protection holds them.
event.protection-override-row-rejected: A stored confirmation did not verify ({why}) and was removed; the protection holds its rule.
event.protection-override-granted: A rule the protection of system programs refuses was confirmed and applies for its term: {rule} ({reason}, {term}).
event.protection-override-expired: A confirmed rule reached the end of its term; the protection holds it again: {rule}.
event.protection-override-delete-failed: An ended confirmation could not be removed from the database; it is not honoured (error: {error}).
event.protection-override-audit-failed: The end of a confirmed rule could not be audited; it ended all the same (error: {error}).
event.protection-override-expiry-unarmed: The timer of a confirmed rule could not start; the rule still ends on time at the next rules read (error: {error}).
event.protection-override-crash-loop: The service stopped unexpectedly several times in a row; every confirmation of a protected rule is withdrawn.
event.protection-override-services-changed: A service account now runs what a confirmed rule takes; the rule waits for a new confirmation: {rule}.
event.service-set-watch-unavailable: Installed services are not watched; confirmed rules are re-checked on a timer (error: {error}).
event.service-set-watch-stopped: The watch on installed services stopped (code {code}); confirmed rules are re-checked on a timer.
event.svc-run-state-write-failed: The start could not be recorded, so repeated unexpected stops would go unnoticed (error: {error}).
event.prod-rules-state-db-mutex-poisoned: State database lock was poisoned; treating as no active rules.
event.prod-rules-get-active-failed: Reading the active revision failed; treating as no active rules (error: {error}).
event.prod-networks-store-decision-failed: Could not store the local-network decision for {cidr} ({error}).
event.prod-networks-prune-superseded-failed: Could not prune superseded local-network answers for adapter {adapter} ({error}).
event.prod-networks-refusing-anchor-store-fail: Could not record that a site refuses main-link addresses ({error}).

event.prod-diag-log-page-duplicate-positions: Log page positions are not unique; paging can drop entries (duplicates: {duplicates}).
event.prod-coord-activation-audit-append-faile: Audit append failed for an activation event (error: {error}).
event.dns-listener-short-name-completed: Completed short name {label} using the network domain, resolving as {completed} from server {server}.
event.dns-listener-modeb-resolves-caught-up: Local DNS resolver:rule-host resolution is keeping up again — answering from the upstream as usual.
event.dns-listener-direct-host-parked-suggesti: {host}, a site outside your rules, is a parked suggestion for the additional route — left there instead of being steered onto the main route.
event.dns-listener-modeb-direct-host-shared-ad: Local DNS resolver: {host}, a site outside your rules, shares its addresses with an additional-route rule — answered so that it stays on the main route.

event.dns-listener-rule-host-ipv6-uncovered: Rule host {host} was queried over IPv6, which this rule cannot cover — its IPv6 traffic leaves outside the rule.
event.dns-listener-modeb-resolve-slots-saturat: Local DNS resolver:all {concurrent} rule-host resolve slots are waiting on an unresponsive upstream — serving rule hosts from the cache so the rest of the machine's DNS keeps working.
event.dns-listener-modeb-unrecognised-recv-err: Local DNS resolver:an unrecognized error occurred while receiving a query ({error}, {consecutive_errors} in a row) — continuing to serve.

event.dns-first-contact-timing: First-contact routes over the last minute: {calls} DNS answers waited on them, {avg_us} µs on average, {max_us} µs at most; {slow} took longer than 5 ms.
event.dns-listener-query-shed: Local DNS resolver:a DNS query from {source} was failed at once instead of queued ({reason}; {shed} so far) — the resolver is saturated or one program is past its share.
event.dns-resolver-withheld-name-leak-guard: Leak protection is blocking: the name of rule host {host} was not sent over the main link ({reason}) — the answer is withheld.
event.dns-resolver-redirect-lifted-no-upstream: Local DNS resolver: no upstream DNS server answers — system DNS is handed back to the OS until one does.
event.dns-resolver-redirect-lifted-only-foreig: Local DNS resolver: only another VPN's DNS server answers — system DNS is handed back to the OS and name-based routing is off until a resolver of ours answers.
event.dns-upstream-dropped-foreign: The upstream DNS server was dropped: its network now belongs to another VPN.
event.dns-resolver-redirect-back-upstream-answ: Local DNS resolver: an upstream DNS server answers again — system DNS is redirected to the resolver.
event.dns-resolver-redirect-refused: Local DNS resolver: the system accepted the DNS redirect and then refused it — it was withdrawn, names resolve past the resolver, and it will be tried again.
event.dns-resolver-tcp-bind-failed: Local DNS resolver: could not listen for DNS over TCP on {addr} ({error}) — answers too large for a datagram will not resolve.
event.dns-stack-modeb-no-signed-in-user: Local DNS resolver:no signed-in user yet — staying in reactive mode until sign-in.
event.dns-stack-modeb-armed: Local DNS resolver on: it ({listener}) forwards non-rule queries to upstream {upstream}, which answered a probe.
event.dns-stack-servers-uncached: Network changes cannot be watched ({error}); every unanswered name re-reads the machine's DNS servers.
event.dns-servers-cache-config-feed-unwatched: DNS configuration changes cannot be watched ({error}); the DNS server list still refreshes when a connection or route changes.
event.dns-stack-changes-unwatched: Network or DNS settings changes cannot be watched ({error}); the local resolver re-reads the connections' DNS domains on every check.
event.dns-stack-short-name-suffixes-unread: The short-name domains could not be read ({error}); the ones read before stay in use.
event.dns-stack-local-suffixes-unread: The home-network suffix list could not be read ({error}); the one read before stays in use.
event.dns-stack-modeb-no-upstream-answered: The local DNS resolver was requested, but no upstream DNS server answered a probe — staying in reactive mode.
event.power-resume-rebind-requested: Re-resolving the adapter binding on request ({reason}).
event.power-resume-from-sleep: The machine resumed from sleep — re-resolving the adapter binding and re-applying routes.
event.prodmisc-failclosed-state: Leak protection blocking traffic for the additional route: {fail_closed_active}.
event.prodmisc-adapter-infos-failed: Could not read adapter information ({error}) — returning an empty snapshot.
event.prodmisc-adapter-enum-empty-placeholder: Live adapter enumeration ({data_source}) produced no rows — answering with the placeholder dataset instead.
event.prodmisc-route-bindings-load-failed: Could not load route bindings for this user ({error}) — the leak protection banner is suppressed.
event.autorules-authored-over-budget: Application-authored rules exceeded the budget of {budget}; dropped the {dropped} oldest (e.g. {sample}) — a site that still needs one will be offered again.
event.autorules-inbox-accepted: Accepted {accepted} suggested address(es) (e.g. {anchor}) — added to the user's own rules.
event.autorules-inbox-accept-failed: Could not add the accepted addresses to the rules (code: {code}): {error}.
event.autorules-inbox-dismissed: Declined {dismissed} suggested address(es) (e.g. {anchor}) — they will not be offered again.
event.enforcement-link-keeps-dropping: A connection keeps dropping for a few seconds and coming back.
event.autorules-inbox-restored: Restored {restored} previously declined address(es); {re_offered} are back on the suggestion list.
event.autorules-inbox-erased: Erased {forgotten} suggestion(s) — they may be offered again from scratch.
event.autorules-intake-evidence-restored: Restored companion evidence from before the last restart: {candidates} candidate(s), {anchors} anchor(s).
event.autorules-intake-not-offered-companion-b: Not offering {host}: every measured sighting came inside another page's burst ({companions} companion(s)).
event.autorules-intake-app-offer-stalled: Offering to move {program} onto the additional route: {stalled} of its connection(s) did not complete on the main link.
event.autorules-intake-app-offer-own-resolver: Offering a rule for {program}: it looks up site names on its own, so rules by site name do not reach {unnamed} of the addresses it used.
event.autorules-intake-domain-offer: A second name under {domain} ({host}) fails on the main link — offering the whole domain instead of each name.
event.autorules-ledger-auto-added: Automatically added {added} address(es) a routed site needs (e.g. {anchor}) to the user's own rules.
event.autorules-ledger-serialize-failed: Could not serialize a pending suggestion ({error}) — it will not survive a restart.
event.autorules-ledger-auto-add-failed: Could not automatically add discovered addresses (e.g. {anchor}, code: {code}): {error}.
event.autorules-pending-cap-dropped: Pending suggestions reached the cap of {kept}; dropped the weakest {dropped}.
event.autorules-store-refused-read-failed: Could not read refused suggestions ({error}) — this session may re-offer a host the user already declined.
event.autorules-store-refused-persist-failed: Could not persist {count} refused suggestion(s) ({error}) — the refusal holds for this session only.
event.autorules-store-declined-read-failed: Could not read declined suggestions for review ({error}).
event.autorules-store-declined-undo-failed: Could not undo a declined suggestion ({error}) — it stays refused for this session.
event.autorules-store-pending-read-failed: Could not read pending suggestions ({error}) — this session starts with an empty offer set.
event.autorules-store-pending-persist-failed: Could not persist {count} pending suggestion(s) ({error}) — they will not survive a restart.
event.autorules-store-pending-clear-failed: Could not clear persisted pending suggestions ({error}).
event.autorules-store-companion-read-failed: Could not read saved companion evidence ({error}) — learning starts over for this session.
event.autorules-store-companion-format-mismatc: Saved companion evidence is not readable by this build ({error}) — starting over.
event.autorules-store-companion-persist-failed: Could not persist companion evidence ({error}) — it will not survive a restart.
event.autorules-store-companion-clear-failed: Could not clear saved companion evidence ({error}).
event.autorules-tick-companion-domain-summary: Companion-domain check found addresses a routed site needs: parked {parked}, authored {authored}, pending {pending}, published {published}.
event.verbose-logging-window-ended: Verbose service logging window ended; back to normal logging.
event.verbose-logging-expiry-unarmed: Verbose logging timer could not start ({error}); the window ends at the next service restart.
event.conn-trace-log-window-ended: Connection trace log window ended; connections are no longer written to the log.
event.conn-trace-log-expiry-unarmed: Connection trace log timer could not start ({error}); the window ends at the next service restart.
event.conn-trace-log-at-boot: Connection trace log at service start: {mode} (until {until_ms}, forced: {forced}).
event.storage-kill-switch-protocols-reset: A stored leak protection protocol selection blocked nothing; every protocol is blocked instead.
event.persid-plan-network-carving-over-cap: {count} network rule(s) hold more narrower rules than can be carved out, so each is not fully enforced and the narrower rules inside keep working ({rules}).
event.linux-flow-reset-dump-capped: The connection table holds more {family} sockets than one listing reads ({cap}); connections past that are not reset.
event.svc-boot-restarted-after-unasked-stop: The service started again after a stop nobody asked for; protection was off in between.
event.svc-scm-stop-unasked: Stopped by something other than NetRuleRouter's own commands; the service will be started again. To keep it stopped, use "nrr-cli stop".
event.svc-scm-stop-with-filtering-engine: Stopping because the Windows Base Filtering Engine is going down; the service will be started again once the engine is back.
event.routingpause-term-read-failed: The ended pauses could not be read; they are tried again: {error}
event.routingpause-term-ended: A pause reached its end and routing resumed
event.routingpause-term-resume-failed: A pause reached its end but routing did not resume; it is tried again: {error}
event.supervised-spawn-routing-pause-term-tick: The task that ends timed pauses did not start: {error}

errors.elevation-agent-missing: Administrator approval could not be asked for: nothing in this session can show the password prompt. The change was not made.

errors.busy-conflict: Service is busy with another operation
errors.service-relocation-failed: The service could not be copied to a folder only administrators can change. Check that the application folder can be read and that there is free space on the system drive, then try again.
errors.activation-not-recorded: The change could not be saved, so it was not applied. The previous rules stay in effect. Review the changes and apply again.
errors.no-last-known-good: There is no earlier version of your rules to roll back to.
errors.revision-not-found: That version of the rules no longer exists.
errors.revision-integrity-rejected: That version of the rules failed the integrity check and was not used.
errors.rules-changed-elsewhere: Your rules were changed somewhere else after they were loaded here, so nothing was applied. Load them again and merge your changes in.
errors.storage-failure: The service could not read or write its rules storage.
errors.not-implemented: This is not available on this system yet.
errors.route-policy-sites-needs-main-route: Routed sites protection works only when the main connection is the default route.
errors.route-policy-placeholder-adapter: This connection is from a sample list, not from this computer. Wait until the background service lists your connections, then choose one.
errors.unsupported-platform: This is not available on this system, so nothing was changed.
errors.precondition-failed: The service cannot do this in its current state. Refresh and try again.
errors.confirmation-expired: The confirmation of these changes expired. Review the changes and apply them again.
errors.confirmation-unknown: The confirmation of these changes is no longer valid. Review the changes and apply them again.
errors.service-degraded: Service is degraded — try again later
errors.recovery-required: After a failure the service stopped taking changes. Restart the service; if it happens again, save a diagnostics archive.
errors.unsupported-operation: The running service is older than this app and does not know this action. Restart the service, or update it, and try again.
errors.response-too-large: The service's answer was too large to send; the change itself may have been applied — refresh before trying again.
errors.settings-export-too-large: Your rules are too many to fit in one settings export. Nothing was written; save your rules as rules files instead.
errors.gui-internal: Internal error in the application — the change was not sent
errors.timeout: The service did not answer in time. Try again.
errors.bad-response: The service answered in a way this app cannot read. Restart the service or update the app.
errors.serialization-failed: The app could not prepare this request. Try again; if it happens again, save a diagnostics archive.
errors.client-shutdown: The app is closing, so the request was not sent.
errors.unknown-operation: The running service is older than this app and does not know this action. Restart the service, or update it, and try again.
errors.unknown-preset-operation: The rules-file export/parse operation isn't available.
errors.rpc-timed-out: The service did not answer in time. Try again.
errors.safe-disable-rpc-pending: Rules cannot be turned off from this window right now: it has no connection to the service. Restart the app and try again.
errors.rules-locked: Your administrator manages the routing rules on this computer, so they cannot be changed here.

errors.network-covers-fake-ip-pool: The network overlaps the address range the program reserves for name-based routing. Choose a different network.

errors.network-covers-fake-ip-pool-named: The network {network} overlaps the address range the program reserves for name-based routing. Choose a different network.
errors.security-alert-unacknowledged: Rules cannot be changed until the security alert in Diagnostics is reviewed and acknowledged.
errors.terminal-needs-elevation-unix: This needs administrator rights, and nrr-tui does not ask for them. Quit and start it again with the command sudo nrr-tui.
errors.terminal-needs-elevation-windows: This needs administrator rights, and nrr-tui does not ask for them. Quit and start it again from a terminal opened with Run as administrator.
errors.revision-status-mismatch: These changes were already applied — nothing was sent again.
errors.token-already-consumed: These changes were already applied — nothing was sent again.
errors.audit-chain-changed: The audit trail changed after the breaks were shown. Nothing was restarted.
errors.audit-chain-intact: The audit chain is intact — there is nothing to restart.
errors.restart-key-unavailable: The service has no integrity key to seal a restart with, so the audit chain cannot be restarted on this computer.
errors.audit-write-failed: The service could not write to the audit trail.
errors.audit-unavailable: The audit trail is not available in the service.

errors.payload-too-large: The file is over the size limit for a rule set.
errors.file-encoding: The file is not saved as UTF-8 text. Save it in UTF-8 and import it again.

errors.match-value-too-long: A value in the file is longer than the limit.
errors.inline-comment-too-long: A comment in the file is longer than the limit.
errors.canonicalize-rejected: A rule in the file does not fit its section, so the file was not imported.
errors.preset-validation-failed: The file could not be checked, so it was not imported.

errors.illegal-state-transition: This alert has already been handled, so it cannot be changed again.

errors.rules-record-not-saved: The service could not save the rules as they are now, so the alert stays open. Try again; if it fails again, export a diagnostics archive.

errors.alerts-store-unavailable: Security alerts are not available in the service.
