unrouted.other: The program {app} is on this computer, but its rule routes none of its traffic.

first-run-needs-admin.title: A setup answer needs an administrator
first-run-needs-admin.body: “{setting}” applies to the whole computer, so only an administrator can turn it on. It stays off for now; an administrator can switch it on in the routing settings.

service-operation-failed.title: Service action failed: {operation}
service-operation-failed.body: The service did not carry out this action, so nothing changed. Open Settings to try again, or check the logs for the reason.

update-available.title: A new version is available
update-available.body: NetRuleRouter {version} has been released (you are running {current}). Open the download page to update.

auto-rule-candidates.title: Addresses waiting to be added
auto-rule-candidates.body: The service found {count} addresses the sites you routed need.

reason.route-unavailable: The route this connection needed was unavailable.
reason.ipv6-blocked: With leak protection set to Everything, IPv6 goes out only through the additional connection, so this connection did not go out.
reason.dns-lockdown: This app went to its own DNS resolver instead of the one NetRuleRouter provides, and encrypted-DNS blocking closed it.
reason.unattributed: NetRuleRouter blocked this connection, but could not identify which filter did it.

backlog.title: Blocked while the app was closed

counted.one: The service blocked {count} connection while NetRuleRouter was not open.
counted.other: The service blocked {count} connections while NetRuleRouter was not open.

unassigned-tunnel.title: The additional route is not assigned
unassigned-tunnel.body: {adapter} is up, but no connection is assigned to the additional route — so the sites your rules send there will not open.

local-network-too-wide.title: This network looks suspicious
local-network-too-wide.body: {adapter} reports {network} as its local network — far wider than any local network can be. It is not treated as local: devices on it stay blocked while leak protection is on, and sites inside it still follow your rules.

local-networks.title: A local network was found
local-networks.body: {cidr} on {adapter} stays reachable while routed traffic is blocked. Keep it that way?
local-networks.body-open: Your home network's IPv6 addresses {cidr} on {adapter} are closed while routed traffic is blocked. Open them to devices on this network?

adapter-choice.title: Choose which adapter to use
adapter-choice.body: Several adapters answer to the saved name, so your rules are not being applied. Pick the one to use: {list}

no-primary.title: Main connection is not set
no-primary.body: Without a main connection there is nowhere to send traffic your rules do not route, so the rules are not being applied.

primary-no-way-out.title: The main connection has no way to the internet
primary-no-way-out.body: The connection chosen as main has no gateway, so traffic your rules do not route is going out the way the system sends it instead. Choose the connection that actually reaches the internet as main.

no-policy.title: Connections are not chosen yet
no-policy.suggest-body: Nothing is routed until you confirm it. Rules for the additional connection wait until you choose one.
no-policy.body: The service has no routing settings for you yet, so nothing is being routed. Choose the main and additional connections.

restored.title: Routing is working again
restored.body: Your rules are being applied again. Pages that were refused while the connection was down keep showing the error until you reload them — press F5 on those tabs.

primary-down.title: The main connection is not up
primary-down.body: Traffic that is not routed to the additional connection has nowhere to go until it comes back. Check the cable, the Wi-Fi, or pick another main connection.

secondary-down.title: The additional connection is not up
secondary-down.body: Everything your rules send there is being held until it comes back — that is the protection doing its job, not a fault. Start the connection, or move those rules to the main one.
secondary-down.body-off: Sites your rules send there go over the main connection until it comes back: leak protection is off. Start the connection, or turn leak protection on to hold them instead.
secondary-down.body-everything: The internet waits until it comes back, except your local network and what your rules send over the main connection — that is the protection doing its job, not a fault. Start the connection.

adapters-unreadable.title: Cannot read the list of connections
adapters-unreadable.body: The service cannot enumerate network adapters right now, so your rules are not being applied. This usually clears itself; if it does not, restart the service.

unknown.title: Your rules are not being applied
unknown.body: The service reported a state this version does not recognise. Open interfaces and routes to check the setup.

adapter-gone.title: The saved connection is gone
adapter-gone.body: The connection your rules were set to use is no longer on this computer, so the rules are not being applied. Pick another one: {list}
adapter-gone.body-empty: The connection your rules were set to use is no longer on this computer, and there is nothing to replace it with right now.

adapter-failed.title: The saved connection is broken
adapter-failed.body: The connection your rules use is still installed, but its driver will not start, so the rules are not being applied. Reinstall it, or pick another one: {list}
adapter-failed.body-empty: The connection your rules use is still installed, but its driver will not start, and there is nothing to replace it with right now. Reinstalling it usually helps.

rules-file-converged.title: Your rules file was brought up to date
rules-file-converged.body: The linked rules file was written differently from the rules in the app, but both described the same routing. The file has been rewritten to match; nothing about what is applied changed.
rules-file-converged.added-body: Rules already in force were missing from your rules file and are now written to it: {rules}. Nothing about what is applied changed.

rules-file-not-written.title: Rules applied, but your rules file was not updated
rules-file-not-written.body: The rules are in force, but writing them to your rules file failed, so the file still holds the previous rules. Use "Save to file" on the Rules screen to try again.

service-refused.title: The service will not accept this app
service-refused.body: The background service is running, but it refused a connection from this account. That usually means the service was installed by a different user, or it is already serving as many connections as it allows. Reinstalling the service as an administrator, or signing in as the account that installed it, restores the link.

rule-duplicates.title: A rule is set on both routes
rule-duplicates.body: {count} of your rules are enabled on both routes, starting with {sample}. Which one carries the traffic is decided by evaluation order.

rule-override-ended.title: The protection holds a rule again
rule-override-ended.body: The term you confirmed has ended for {rules}. The rule is not applied until you confirm it again in the rules list.

rule-override-withdrawn.title: Confirmations were withdrawn
rule-override-withdrawn.body: Confirmations of protected rules were withdrawn: the service stopped unexpectedly several times in a row. The rules are not applied until you confirm them again in the rules list.

rule-override-recheck.title: A rule needs a new confirmation
rule-override-recheck.body: A service now runs what {rules} takes, which your confirmation did not cover. The rule is not applied until you confirm it again in the rules list.

app-rule-learning.title: New application rule is settling in
app-rule-learning.body: {apps}: the service is still learning which addresses this program uses, so its first connection attempts may fail. Restart the program if it is already open.

settings-unreadable.title: Your settings could not be read
settings-unreadable.body: This session uses default settings and will not save changes, so your saved settings stay as they are. Close the app and open it again; if the file is locked by another program, free it first.

tui-settings-damaged.title: The terminal's settings file is damaged
tui-settings-damaged.body: This session uses default settings and does not save changes, so {path} is left as it is: correct or delete it, and saving works again.

tui-settings-unreadable.title: The terminal's settings file could not be read
tui-settings-unreadable.body: This session uses default settings and does not save changes, so {path} is left as it is. If another program holds the file or its permissions shut you out, free it, and saving works again.

user-settings-damaged.title: Your settings file is damaged
user-settings-damaged.body: This window keeps the settings it has. Until the file is fixed, changes to your rule-set folder, bound rules files and other shared settings do not reach the terminal or the tray, and theirs do not reach this window. The file is left as it is: correct or delete it, and the window reads it again by itself.

delivery-incomplete.title: The installation is incomplete
delivery-incomplete.body: This copy of the program lacks {parts}. Everything else keeps working. Reinstall the program to restore what is missing.

part.locales: the interface languages, so the program is shown in English
part.service-binary: the background service, so it cannot be installed or started from this window

vpn-client-trust.title: Is this your VPN?
vpn-client-trust.body: {name} looks like a VPN client, but it is not installed in a protected program folder, so leak protection does not trust it on its own. Confirm it and it will keep working while leak protection is on.

body-bundle.one: {name} looks like a VPN client, but it is not installed in a protected program folder, so leak protection does not trust it on its own. It ships with {count} more program that can be trusted with it.
body-bundle.other: {name} looks like a VPN client, but it is not installed in a protected program folder, so leak protection does not trust it on its own. It ships with {count} more programs that can be trusted with it.

vpn-client-trust.action-bundle: This is my VPN, with the programs it ships with
vpn-client-trust.tray-body: {apps} looks like a VPN client, but it is not installed in a protected program folder. Open NetRuleRouter to confirm it, or leak protection keeps blocking it while the additional route is down.
vpn-client-trust.tui-body: {apps}: named like a VPN client, but not installed in a protected program folder, so leak protection does not trust it on its own.
vpn-client-trust.tui-hint: t: confirm {name} as your VPN. The other programs are asked one at a time after it.
vpn-client-trust.tui-hint-bundle: t: confirm {name} as your VPN. T: confirm it together with the {count} program(s) it ships with in its protected folder. The other programs are asked one at a time after it.
vpn-client-trust.tui-done: {count} program(s) confirmed as your VPN; leak protection keeps them working over the main link.
vpn-client-trust.tui-failed: Could not save the confirmation to the routing service ({error}).

vpn-gateway-trust.title: Let this VPN connect?
vpn-gateway-trust.body: Leak protection stopped a VPN from reaching its server {address} over your main connection. Allow it and that VPN connects while leak protection is on; nothing else is let through to that address.
vpn-gateway-trust.body-program: Leak protection stopped {name} from reaching the VPN server {address} over your main connection. Allow it and that VPN connects while leak protection is on; nothing else is let through to that address.
vpn-gateway-trust.tray-body: A VPN is waiting for your answer in the NetRuleRouter window: leak protection stopped it from reaching its server {addresses}.

protection-restored.title: Protection restored after a service failure
protection-restored.body: The service had lost these settings and they were switched back on: {settings}.

service-lost.title: The service stopped
service-lost.body: The NetRuleRouter service stopped unexpectedly, so your rules are not applied. Start it again, or restore network access if the connection is cut.
service-lost.body-start-only: The NetRuleRouter service stopped unexpectedly, so your rules are not applied.

rules-book-unreadable.title: Your saved rules cannot be read
rules-book-unreadable.body: Your saved rules cannot be read; the last applied rules stay in force. Changes will not apply until this is fixed.
rules-book-unreadable.cleared: Your saved rules can be read again; changes apply again.

system-dns-not-restored.title: Sites may not open by name
system-dns-not-restored.body: NetRuleRouter could not hand the system DNS settings back. Restore network removes what the service left behind.

dns-foreign-only.title: Name handling is paused by your VPN
dns-foreign-only.body: Your work VPN only lets its own DNS answer, so NetRuleRouter's name handling is paused until another DNS answers. Rules by site name may not apply meanwhile. Disconnect the VPN, or ask its administrator to allow other DNS servers.

host-unreachable.title: A site does not answer on either link
host-unreachable.body: {host} did not answer through the main link or through the additional one, so moving it would not help and nothing was offered. The problem is most likely on the site's side.

routes-held.title: Some addresses follow another user's route
routes-held.body: Another user signed in to this computer already routes some addresses from your rules through a different connection. Addresses affected: {count}. While that user stays signed in, these addresses follow their route, or are blocked for you if leak protection is on. Among them: {list}.
routes-held.cleared: Addresses from your rules follow your own route again.

traffic-carried.title: Your traffic goes through another user's tunnel
traffic-carried.body: Another user of this computer signed in earlier and sends all their traffic through the tunnel "{link}". This computer has one route table for everyone, so whatever your rules do not send to your additional connection goes through that tunnel too. To avoid this, sign in before that user, or ask them to send only chosen sites through their tunnel.
traffic-carried.body-unnamed: Another user of this computer signed in earlier and sends all their traffic through their tunnel. This computer has one route table for everyone, so whatever your rules do not send to your additional connection goes through that tunnel too. To avoid this, sign in before that user, or ask them to send only chosen sites through their tunnel.
traffic-carried.cleared: Your traffic no longer goes through another user's tunnel.

settings-lost.title: The service does not have your settings
settings-lost.body: This happens after the service was reinstalled or its data was reset. Missing: {settings}.

forwarded-traffic.title: WSL or containers are running
forwarded-traffic.body: Choose what WSL, containers and virtual machines get when the additional route goes down. Until you choose, they are protected like this computer.

connection-reset.title: Closing connections after a rule change
connection-reset.effect: Connections opened before a rule change stay on their previous route until they close.

user-routes.title: Separate routes per user
user-routes.effect: All users share one route; per-user routing needs Linux 4.10 or newer.

block-reports.title: Reports of blocked connections
block-reports.effect: Blocks are enforced, but blocked-site notices and the outage list stay empty.

ipsec-networks.title: Corporate IPsec networks under full leak protection
ipsec-networks.effect: With leak protection set to Everything, a strongSwan or libreswan connection without a network interface of its own cannot reach its company's networks. This needs Linux 4.20 and nftables 0.9.1 or newer.

foreign-rule-ahead.title: A routing rule of another program comes first
foreign-rule-ahead.effect: A catch-all rule of another program (often a VPN) is looked up before ours, so some traffic may bypass the routes you set.

dns-foreign-catch-all.title: Another program takes over name lookups
dns-foreign-catch-all.effect: Another program (often a VPN or a security tool) sends every site name to its own DNS server, so site rules may miss some sites. Close that program or turn off its DNS setting.

block-reason.dns-lockdown: Blocks of apps using their own DNS

app-groups.intro: A whole group of programs, or the machines of a hypervisor, can be sent over the main or the additional route at once. Changes go to your rules list, where you review and apply them.
app-groups.no-rules: Your rules have not been read yet, so a route cannot be assigned. Connect to the service first.
app-groups.unchanged: The rules already send it that way. Nothing changed.
app-groups.not-assignable: Item {n} cannot be given a route: no program rule reaches its traffic.
app-groups.locked: The rules list is being applied and cannot change meanwhile.
app-groups.not-hypervisor: Item {n} is not a hypervisor, so it has no machines to show.
app-groups.no-target: There is no adapter {n} that can be tied to a route.
app-groups.pin-busy: The previous change to a machine is still being made.
app-groups.pin-unchanged: The adapter is already set that way. Nothing changed.

service.dns-not-restored: System DNS could not be restored. Run nrr-cli reset-network as administrator.

suggestions.loading: Reading the suggestions from the service...

suggestions.no-item: There is no item {n} in the list. Use the number shown before an item.
suggestions.item-gone: Item {n} as it was listed is no longer offered. Here is the list as it is now.
suggestions.nothing-to-do: Item {n} has nothing this command can act on.

suggestions.confirm-prompt: Type y to turn it on or n to cancel, then press Enter.
suggestions.forgotten: Forgotten with their answers: {count}. They can be offered again if they turn up beside your sites.
suggestions.clear-confirm: y: forget all {count} suggestions together with your answers. n: cancel.

overlaps.pairs-title: Rules that cover the same sites
overlaps.apply-on-rules: Review and apply the change on screen {key}, {screen}.
overlaps.loading: Reading your rules from the service...
overlaps.no-item: There is no item {n} in the list. Use the number shown before an item.
overlaps.cannot-send: Item {n} cannot be sent over the other route here; change it in the rules list.
overlaps.gone: The rules of item {n} changed in the meantime; nothing was sent.

list.more-on-service: The service has more: going past the last row asks for them.
list.help-pages: PageUp and PageDown: previous and next page; Home and End: first and last row
list.plain-pages: n: next page (more)   p: previous page (back)
list.help-refresh: r: read again from the service. Lists do not refresh by themselves, so nothing moves while you read.

trace.help-explain: Enter: why the chosen connection took its route (opens Diagnostics)
trace.help-search: /: search all fields; Enter applies the search, Esc cancels

trace.plain-details: d and a row number: show that connection, for example d 3
trace.plain-explain: e and a row number: why that connection took its route, for example e 3

trace.plain-check-site: c and a row number: check that connection's site, for example c 3

trace.plain-grouping: g: the next grouping; g none, g program or g folder: that grouping; f and a row number: a rule for that row's folder, for example f 3

outage-blocks.where: The list of what was blocked: {screen}

cache.clear-app-question: Clear the app cache? Names are resolved again as programs use them.
cache.clear-os-question: Flush the operating system's DNS cache?

cache.help-clear: c: clear the app cache   o: flush the operating system's DNS cache (each asks first)
cache.help-filters: f: freshness, t: source, w: route; each press shows the next choice of that filter
cache.help-seed: b: seed the cache from browser history (only names that match your rules)
cache.plain-details: d and a row number: show that entry, for example d 3
cache.plain-search: / and text: search the cache on the service, for example /example.com; / on its own clears the search

diagnostics.archive-unreadable: The service wrote the archive, but this account cannot open it.
diagnostics.help-switch: l: switch between diagnostics, the log and the audit trail
diagnostics.help-ack: Up and Down: choose an alert; a: acknowledge it
diagnostics.help-explain: e: type a host name or address and see which rule decides it
diagnostics.help-export: x: export a diagnostic archive; the service writes it and the path is shown here
diagnostics.help-log-filters: In the log: v changes the lowest level shown, / filters by event type, s switches between this session and all history

diagnostics.site-trace: t: open the connection trace to see what the site's connections did
diagnostics.plain-log-filters: In the log: v next level, / and text filter by event type (/ on its own clears), s this session or all history

connection.fix-restore-network: To restore the network, run: {command} (leak protection stays off until the service applies its rules again)
connection.fix-stop-and-restore-network: To stop the service and restore the network, run: {command} (leak protection stays off until the service is started again)
connection.versions: The service speaks protocol version {server}, this program version {client}. Update NetRuleRouter so both match.
connection.ssh-only-session: Signed in over SSH: your rules are saved but apply only while you are also signed in to Windows.

status.vpn-gateway-allowed-many: The VPN servers {addresses} can now be reached while leak protection is on.

status.block-route-already: {name} already goes over the additional route; nothing was added.
status.block-route-failed: Could not send {name} over the additional route: {error}

help.move: Up and Down: move through the list
help.panels: Tab and Shift+Tab: move between panels
help.open: Enter: open the screen chosen in the list
help.help: F1 or ?: help for this screen
help.back: Esc: back, or close this help

help.feed-site: A notification about a site that does not open offers c: check whether the network or the site is at fault (opens Diagnostics).
help.status-vpn-trust: t: confirm the first listed program as your VPN (T: with the programs it ships with), so leak protection keeps it working
help.status-vpn-gateway: a: allow the first listed VPN to reach its server, so leak protection lets it connect
help.status-block-route: v: send the blocked site named under the state over the additional route; you are asked first

help.settings-esc: Esc: cancel a change, or go back to the list of sections.

plain.help-enter: Enter on its own: show this screen again
